newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Annan keeps up efforts to assemble Zaire force.
newsitem.headline: Annan keeps up efforts to assemble Zaire force.

text.p: U.N. Secretary General Kofi Annan said on Tuesday efforts to assemble a humanitarian force to help refugees in Zaire remained one of his top priorities.
"I'm on my way to New York tonight and one of the first things I will be focusing on will be how we get assistance and mobilise ourselves to assist the refugees," he said.

Annan was speaking on the final day of a three-day trip to the Netherlands where he has met Dutch government leaders and top officials at the International Court of Justice and the International Criminal Tribunal for former Yugoslavia.
He said he hoped an international humanitarian force could be deployed quickly in Zaire.
"If we don't deploy very quickly...within the next few weeks, it may be too late," he told reporters.

Several countries had planned to send troops to Zaire late last year but that plan collapsed when many of an estimated 1.2 million refugees from neighbouring Rwanda and Burundi returned home of their own accord.

However, hundreds of thousands of refugees remain trapped in eastern Zaire with little food or water. Many have been caught up in the fighting in eastern Zaire which began in October between Zairean government troops and rebel forces.

Diplomatic sources said the creation of a new multinational force for Zaire would require a large country to step forward and take on the leadership role which Canada had originally volunteered for when the idea was first mooted.
